An AI coding agent can run the mechanical parts of the upgrade, inspect the diff, fix follow-up breakages, and verify the app. The prompt below asks the agent to read version-matched docs, use the codemods where appropriate, explain important changes, and verify the result. Some runtime verification tools are only available after the app is upgraded.

{/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `<PagesOnly>Content</PagesOnly>` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */}

## Use an AI agent (recommended)

An AI coding agent can run the mechanical parts of the upgrade, inspect the diff, fix follow-up breakages, and verify the app. The prompt below asks the agent to read version-matched docs, use the codemods where appropriate, explain important changes, and verify the result. Some runtime verification tools are only available after the app is upgraded.

Give the agent this prompt:

```prompt
Upgrade this app to Next.js 16.

Before editing code, make sure AGENTS.md points at version-matched Next.js docs. If it is missing or outdated, follow [Set up AI agent docs](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#set-up-ai-agent-docs), then read AGENTS.md.

Then follow the [Next.js 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16) as the source of truth for the migration. Use the [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#using-the-codemod) when you're ready to run the mechanical upgrade.

title: not-found.js
description: API reference for the not-found.js file.
---

Next.js provides two conventions to handle not found cases:

- **`not-found.js`**: Used when you call the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function in a route segment.
- **`global-not-found.js`**: Used to define a global 404 page for unmatched routes across your entire app. This is handled at the routing level and doesn't depend on rendering a layout or page.

## `not-found.js`

The **not-found** file is used to render UI when the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function is thrown within a route segment. Along with serving a custom UI, Next.js will return a `200` HTTP status code for streamed responses, and `404` for non-streamed responses (see [Status Codes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#status-codes) for details about SEO).

title: not-found.js
description: API reference for the not-found.js file.
---

Next.js provides two conventions to handle not found cases:

- **`not-found.js`**: Used when you call the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function in a route segment.
- **`global-not-found.js`**: Used to define a global 404 page for unmatched routes across your entire app. This is handled at the routing level and doesn't depend on rendering a layout or page.

## `not-found.js`

The **not-found** file is used to render UI when the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function is thrown within a route segment. Along with serving a custom UI, Next.js will return a `200` HTTP status code for streamed responses, and `404` for non-streamed responses (see [Status Codes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#status-codes) for details about SEO).

00003| description: API reference for the useRouter hook.
00004| ---
00005| 
00006| The `useRouter` hook allows you to programmatically change routes inside [Client Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components).
00007| 
00008| > **Recommendation:** Use the [`<Link>` component](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) for navigation unless you have a specific requirement for using `useRouter`.
00009| 
00010| ```tsx filename="app/example-client-component.tsx" switcher
00011| 'use client'
00012| 
00013| import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
00014| 
00015| export default function Page() {
00016|   const router = useRouter()
00017| 
00018|   return (
00019|     <button type="button" onClick={() => router.push('/dashboard')}>
00020|       Dashboard
00021|     </button>
00022|   )
00023| }
00024| ```
00025| 
00026| ```jsx filename="app/example-client-component.js" switcher
00027| 'use client'
00028| 
00029| import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
00030| 
00031| export default function Page() {
00032|   const router = useRouter()
00033| 
00034|   return (
00035|     <button type="button" onClick={() => router.push('/dashboard')}>
00036|       Dashboard
00037|     </button>
00038|   )
00039| }
00040| ```
00041| 
00042| ## `useRouter()`
00043| 
00044| - `router.push(href: string, { scroll: boolean, transitionTypes: string[] })`: Perform a client-side navigation to the provided route. Adds a new entry into the [browser's history stack](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/History_API). The optional `transitionTypes` are passed to [`React.addTransitionType`](https://react.dev/reference/react/addTransitionType) inside the navigation Transition.
00045| - `router.replace(href: string, { scroll: boolean, transitionTypes: string[] })`: Perform a client-side navigation to the provided route without adding a new entry into the browser’s history stack. The optional `transitionTypes` are passed to [`React.addTransitionType`](https://react.dev/reference/react/addTransitionType) inside the navigation Transition.
00046| - `router.refresh()`: Refresh the current route. Making a new request to the server, re-fetching data requests, and re-rendering Server Components. The client will merge the updated React Server Component payload without losing unaffected client-side React (e.g. `useState`) or browser state (e.g. scroll position). This clears the [Client Cache](/docs/app/glossary#client-cache) for the current route, but does **not** invalidate the server-side cache. Use [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) to invalidate server-side cached data.
00047| - `router.prefetch(href: string, options?: { onInvalidate?: () => void })`: [Prefetch](/docs/app/getting-started/linking-and-navigating#prefetching) the provided route for faster client-side transitions. The optional `onInvalidate` callback is called when the [prefetched data becomes stale](/docs/app/guides/prefetching#extending-or-ejecting-link).
00048| - `router.back()`: Navigate back to the previous route in the browser’s history stack.
00049| - `router.forward()`: Navigate forwards to the next page in the browser’s history stack.
00050| - `router.bfcacheId`: An opaque string identifier scoped to the current route segment. It changes when the surrounding segment is freshly created by a push or replace navigation, and stays the same for back/forward navigations, `router.refresh()`, and search-param- or hash-only navigations. See [`bfcacheId`](#bfcacheid) below for details.
00051| 
00052| > **Good to know**:
00053| >
00054| > - You must not send untrusted or unsanitized URLs to `router.push` or `router.replace`, as this can open your site to cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities. For example, `javascript:` URLs sent to `router.push` or `router.replace` will be executed in the context of your page.
00055| > - The `<Link>` component automatically prefetch routes as they become visible in the viewport.
00056| > - `refresh()` could re-produce the same result if fetch requests are cached. Other Request-time APIs like `cookies` and `headers` could also change the response.
00057| > - The `onInvalidate` callback is called at most once per prefetch request. It signals when you may want to trigger a new prefetch for updated route data.
00058| 
00059| ### Migrating from `next/router`
00060| 
00061| - The `useRouter` hook should be imported from `next/navigation` and not `next/router` when using the App Router
00062| - The `pathname` string has been removed and is replaced by [`usePathname()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-pathname)
00063| - The `query` object has been removed and is replaced by [`useSearchParams()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params)
00064| - `router.events` has been replaced. [See below.](#router-events)
00065| 
00066| [View the full migration guide](/docs/app/guides/migrating/app-router-migration).
00067| 
00068| ## Examples
00069| 
00070| ### Router events
00071| 
00072| You can listen for page changes by composing other Client Component hooks like `usePathname` and `useSearchParams`.
00073| 
00074| ```jsx filename="app/components/navigation-events.js"
00075| 'use client'
00076| 
00077| import { useEffect } from 'react'
00078| import { usePathname, useSearchParams } from 'next/navigation'
00079| 
00080| export function NavigationEvents() {
00081|   const pathname = usePathname()
00082|   const searchParams = useSearchParams()
00083| 
00084|   useEffect(() => {
00085|     const url = `${pathname}?${searchParams}`
00086|     console.log(url)
00087|     // You can now use the current URL
00088|     // ...
00089|   }, [pathname, searchParams])
00090| 
00091|   return '...'
00092| }
00093| ```
00094| 
00095| Which can be imported into a layout.
00096| 
00097| ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" highlight={2,10-12}
00098| import { Suspense } from 'react'
00099| import { NavigationEvents } from './components/navigation-events'
00100| 
00101| export default function Layout({ children }) {
00102|   return (
00103|     <html lang="en">
00104|       <body>
00105|         {children}
00106| 
00107|         <Suspense fallback={null}>
00108|           <NavigationEvents />
00109|         </Suspense>
00110|       </body>
00111|     </html>
00112|   )
00113| }
00114| ```
00115| 
00116| > **Good to know**: `<NavigationEvents>` is wrapped in a [`Suspense` boundary](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#examples) because[`useSearchParams()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params) causes client-side rendering up to the closest `Suspense` boundary during [prerendering](/docs/app/glossary#prerendering). [Learn more](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params#behavior).
00117| 
00118| ### Disabling scroll to top
00119| 
00120| By default, Next.js will scroll to the top of the page when navigating to a new route. You can disable this behavior by passing `scroll: false` to `router.push()` or `router.replace()`.

00048|   )

00058| Layout components should accept and use a `children` prop. During rendering, `children` will be populated with the route segments the layout is wrapping. 00079| }

title: Route Segment Config

The Route Segment Config options allow you to configure the behavior of a [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), [Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout), or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) by directly exporting the following variables:

| Option                                                                                             | Type                                                              | Default                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams)     | `boolean`                                                         | `true`                     |
| [`runtime`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/runtime)                 | `'nodejs' \| 'edge' (deprecated)`                                 | `'nodejs'`                 |
| [`preferredRegion`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/preferredRegion) | `'auto' \| 'global' \| 'home' \| string \| string[] (deprecated)` | `'auto'`                   |
| [`maxDuration`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/maxDuration)         | `number`                                                          | Set by deployment platform |

## Version History

| Version      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v16.0.0`    | `dynamic`, `dynamicParams`, `revalidate`, and `fetchCache` removed when [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled. See [Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#route-segment-config). |
| `v16.0.0`    | `export const experimental_ppr = true` removed. A [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#remove-experimental_ppr-route-segment-config-from-app-router-pages-and-layouts) is available.                                                                                                  |

00018| 
00019| The Metadata APIs can be used to define your application metadata for improved SEO and web shareability and include:
00020| 
00021| 1. [The static `metadata` object](#static-metadata)
00022| 2. [The dynamic `generateMetadata` function](#generated-metadata)
00023| 3. Special [file conventions](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata) that can be used to add static or dynamically generated [favicons](#favicons) and [OG images](#static-open-graph-images).
00024| 
00025| With all the options above, Next.js will automatically generate the relevant `<head>` tags for your page, which can be inspected in the browser's developer tools.
00026| 
00027| The `metadata` object and `generateMetadata` function exports are only supported in Server Components.
00028| 
00029| ## Default fields
00030| 
00031| There are two default `meta` tags that are always added even if a route doesn't define metadata:
00032| 
00033| - The [meta charset tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Element/meta#attr-charset) sets the character encoding for the website.
00034| - The [meta viewport tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Viewport_meta_tag) sets the viewport width and scale for the website to adjust for different devices.
00035| 
00036| ```html
00037| <meta charset="utf-8" />
00038| <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
00039| ```
00040| 
00041| The other metadata fields can be defined with the `Metadata` object (for [static metadata](#static-metadata)) or the `generateMetadata` function (for [generated metadata](#generated-metadata)).
00042| 
00043| ## Static metadata
00044| 
00045| To define static metadata, export a [`Metadata` object](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#metadata-object) from a static [`layout.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) or [`page.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) file. For example, to add a title and description to the blog route:
00046| 
00047| ```tsx filename="app/blog/layout.tsx" switcher
00048| import type { Metadata } from 'next'
00049| 
00050| export const metadata: Metadata = {
00051|   title: 'My Blog',
00052|   description: '...',
00053| }
00054| 
00055| export default function Layout() {}
00056| ```
00057| 
00058| ```jsx filename="app/blog/layout.js" switcher
00059| export const metadata = {
00060|   title: 'My Blog',
00061|   description: '...',
00062| }
00063| 
00064| export default function Layout() {}
00065| ```
00066| 
00067| You can view a full list of available options, in the [`generateMetadata` documentation](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#metadata-fields).
00068| 
00069| ## Generated metadata
00070| 
00071| You can use [`generateMetadata`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata) function to `fetch` metadata that depends on data. For example, to fetch the title and description for a specific blog post:
00072| 
00073| ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00074| import type { Metadata, ResolvingMetadata } from 'next'
00075| 
00076| type Props = {
00077|   params: Promise<{ slug: string }>

00004| description: Learn how to cache and revalidate data using fetch options, unstable_cache, and route segment configs for projects not using Cache Components.
00005| ---
00006| 
00007| > This guide assumes you are **not** using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) which was introduced in version 16 under the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents).
00008| 
00009| ## Caching `fetch` requests
00010| 
00011| By default, [`fetch`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch) requests are not cached. You can cache individual requests by setting the `cache` option to `'force-cache'`.
00012| 
00013| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
00014| export default async function Page() {
00015|   const data = await fetch('https://...', { cache: 'force-cache' })
00016| }
00017| ```
00018| 
00019| ```jsx filename="app/page.jsx" switcher
00020| export default async function Page() {
00021|   const data = await fetch('https://...', { cache: 'force-cache' })
00022| }
00023| ```
00024| 
00025| See the [`fetch` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch) to learn more.
00026| 
00027| ### `unstable_cache` for non-`fetch` functions
00028| 
00029| `unstable_cache` allows you to cache the result of database queries and other async functions that don't use `fetch`. Wrap `unstable_cache` around the function:
00030| 
00031| ```ts filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher
00032| import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache'
00033| import { db } from '@/lib/db'
00034| 
00035| export const getCachedUser = unstable_cache(
00036|   async (id: string) => {
00037|     return db
00038|       .select()
00039|       .from(users)
00040|       .where(eq(users.id, id))
00041|       .then((res) => res[0])
00042|   },
00043|   ['user'], // cache key prefix
00044|   {
00045|     tags: ['user'],
00046|     revalidate: 3600,
00047|   }
00048| )
00049| ```
00050| 
00051| ```js filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher
00052| import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache'
00053| import { db } from '@/lib/db'
00054| 
00055| export const getCachedUser = unstable_cache(
00056|   async (id) => {
00057|     return db
00058|       .select()
00059|       .from(users)
00060|       .where(eq(users.id, id))
00061|       .then((res) => res[0])
00062|   },
00063|   ['user'], // cache key prefix
00064|   {
00065|     tags: ['user'],
00066|     revalidate: 3600,
00067|   }
00068| )
00069| ```
00070| 
00071| The third argument accepts:
00072| 
00073| - `tags`: an array of tags for on-demand revalidation with `revalidateTag`.
00074| - `revalidate`: the number of seconds before the cache is revalidated.
00075| 
00076| See the [`unstable_cache` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_cache) to learn more.
00077| 
00078| ### Route segment config
00079| 
00080| You can configure caching behavior at the route level by exporting config options from a [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), [Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout), or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
00081| 
00082| #### `dynamic`
00083| 
00084| Change the dynamic behavior of a layout or page to fully static or fully dynamic.
00085| 
00086| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts" switcher
00087| export const dynamic = 'auto'
00088| // 'auto' | 'force-dynamic' | 'error' | 'force-static'
00089| ```
00090| 
00091| ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
00092| export const dynamic = 'auto'
00093| // 'auto' | 'force-dynamic' | 'error' | 'force-static'
00094| ```
00095| 
00096| - **`'auto'`** (default): The default option to cache as much as possible without preventing any components from opting into dynamic behavior.
00097| - **`'force-dynamic'`**: Force [dynamic rendering](/docs/app/glossary#dynamic-rendering), which will result in routes being rendered for each user at request time. This option is equivalent to:
00098|   - Setting the option of every `fetch()` request in a layout or page to `{ cache: 'no-store', next: { revalidate: 0 } }`.
00099|   - Setting the segment config to `export const fetchCache = 'force-no-store'`
00100| - **`'error'`**: Force prerendering and cache the data of a layout or page by causing an error if any components use Request-time APIs or uncached data. This option is equivalent to:
00101|   - `getStaticProps()` in the `pages` directory.
00102|   - Setting the option of every `fetch()` request in a layout or page to `{ cache: 'force-cache' }`.
00103|   - Setting the segment config to `fetchCache = 'only-cache'`.
00104| - **`'force-static'`**: Force prerendering and cache the data of a layout or page by forcing [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies), [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) and [`useSearchParams()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params) to return empty values. It is possible to [`revalidate`](#route-segment-config-revalidate), [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath), or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag), in pages or layouts rendered with `force-static`.
00105| 
00106| #### `fetchCache`
00107| 
00108| <details>
00109|   <summary>This is an advanced option that should only be used if you specifically need to override the default behavior.</summary>
00110| 
00111| A `fetch` request that sets no `cache` option is fetched once during `next build` if it is reachable **before** any Request-time APIs are used, because the route is prerendered up to that point. Requests discovered **after** a Request-time API run on every request.
00112| 
00113| `fetchCache` allows you to override the default `cache` option of all `fetch` requests in a layout or page.
00114| 
00115| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts" switcher
00116| export const fetchCache = 'auto'
00117| // 'auto' | 'default-cache' | 'only-cache'
00118| // 'force-cache' | 'force-no-store' | 'default-no-store' | 'only-no-store'
00119| ```

00080| You can configure caching behavior at the route level by exporting config options from a [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), [Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout), or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
00081| 
00082| #### `dynamic`
00083| 
00084| Change the dynamic behavior of a layout or page to fully static or fully dynamic.
00085| 
00086| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts" switcher
00087| export const dynamic = 'auto'
00088| // 'auto' | 'force-dynamic' | 'error' | 'force-static'
00089| ```
00090| 
00091| ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
00092| export const dynamic = 'auto'
00093| // 'auto' | 'force-dynamic' | 'error' | 'force-static'
00094| ```
00095| 
00096| - **`'auto'`** (default): The default option to cache as much as possible without preventing any components from opting into dynamic behavior.
00097| - **`'force-dynamic'`**: Force [dynamic rendering](/docs/app/glossary#dynamic-rendering), which will result in routes being rendered for each user at request time. This option is equivalent to:
00098|   - Setting the option of every `fetch()` request in a layout or page to `{ cache: 'no-store', next: { revalidate: 0 } }`.
00099|   - Setting the segment config to `export const fetchCache = 'force-no-store'`
00100| - **`'error'`**: Force prerendering and cache the data of a layout or page by causing an error if any components use Request-time APIs or uncached data. This option is equivalent to:
00101|   - `getStaticProps()` in the `pages` directory.
00102|   - Setting the option of every `fetch()` request in a layout or page to `{ cache: 'force-cache' }`.
00103|   - Setting the segment config to `fetchCache = 'only-cache'`.
00104| - **`'force-static'`**: Force prerendering and cache the data of a layout or page by forcing [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies), [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) and [`useSearchParams()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params) to return empty values. It is possible to [`revalidate`](#route-segment-config-revalidate), [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath), or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag), in pages or layouts rendered with `force-static`.
00105| 
00106| #### `fetchCache`
00107| 
00108| <details>
00109|   <summary>This is an advanced option that should only be used if you specifically need to override the default behavior.</summary>
00110| 
00111| A `fetch` request that sets no `cache` option is fetched once during `next build` if it is reachable **before** any Request-time APIs are used, because the route is prerendered up to that point. Requests discovered **after** a Request-time API run on every request.
00112| 
00113| `fetchCache` allows you to override the default `cache` option of all `fetch` requests in a layout or page.
00114| 
00115| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts" switcher
00116| export const fetchCache = 'auto'
00117| // 'auto' | 'default-cache' | 'only-cache'
00118| // 'force-cache' | 'force-no-store' | 'default-no-store' | 'only-no-store'
00119| ```

 *
 * This file is shipped INTO the sandbox by the orchestrator and executed there as
 * `node __agent_eval__/run.mjs '<AgentRunInput JSON>'`. It is intentionally
 * ZERO-DEPENDENCY (only `node:*` builtins) because the sandbox only has the
 * fixture's own deps + the installed `opencode` CLI — it cannot import anything
 * from the @vercel/agent-eval package.
 *
 * Dual mode:
 *   - runnable: invoked directly → reads argv, runs the agent, writes the result
 *     file + prints a status line, exits 0.
 *   - importable: `import { runAgent } from './run.mjs'` → returns a RunnerResult
 *     (no file write, no exit). This is what a future in-sandbox judge reuses.
 *
 * The pure helpers below are exported (not just `runAgent`) so they can be

 */

events.content:
Migration complete. `pages/` is fully removed; everything now lives in `app/` as TypeScript, verified with `next typegen`, `tsc --noEmit`, `next build`, and a runtime smoke test of every route.

**What changed:**

| Pages Router | App Router replacement |
|---|---|
| `pages/_app.js` + `_document.js` | `app/layout.tsx` — root layout with `<html>/<body>`, `metadata` export, `next/font/google` Inter, global CSS, `AppProvider` |
| `pages/index.js` (`getServerSideProps`) | `app/page.tsx` — async Server Component, `await headers()` for user-agent, `fetch(..., { cache: 'no-store' })` |
| `pages/blog/index.js` (`getStaticProps` + `revalidate: 60`) | `app/blog/page.tsx` — `fetch(..., { next: { revalidate: 60 } })` |
| `pages/blog/[id].js` (`getStaticPaths`/`getStaticProps`) | `app/blog/[id]/page.tsx` — `generateStaticParams`, `next: { revalidate: 300 }`, `dynamicParams = true` (replaces `fallback: 'blocking'`), `notFound()` (replaces `notFound: true`), `generateMetadata`, plus `loading.tsx` (replaces `router.isFallback`) |
| `pages/404.js` | `app/not-found.tsx` |
| `pages/_error.js` | `app/error.tsx` + `app/global-error.tsx` (client boundaries with `retry`) |
| `pages/api/posts/*.js` | `app/api/posts/route.ts` + `app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts` — named `GET`/`POST`/`PUT`/`DELETE` exports, Web `Request`/`Response` APIs, automatic 405 |

**Key API updates per the Next.js 16 docs:**
- `next/router` → `next/navigation` `useRouter` in `'use client'` components (`view-all-posts-button.tsx`, `read-more-button.tsx`, `back-button.tsx`, `go-home-button.tsx`)
- `next/head` → `metadata`/`generateMetadata` exports
- `params` is now a `Promise` (awaited); `headers()` is async
- Types throughout: generated `PageProps<'/blog/[id]'>`, `LayoutProps<'/'>`, `RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>` helpers, `Metadata`, and shared `Post`/`Comment` interfaces in `lib/types.ts`

Build output confirms correct rendering: `/` dynamic, `/blog` ISR 60s, `/blog/[id]` SSG (10 paths) + 5m revalidate. Note: `/blog/999` renders the 404 UI with a 200 status because `loading.tsx` streams the shell first — documented App Router behavior.
